Reviewing my previous response and the peer responses, all the calculations and logical paths align correctly. 

1. Initial total capacity = 1000 beds.
2. Initially occupied = $1/5$ of 1000 = 200 beds.
3. Total admissions over 2 weeks (14 days) = $50 \times 14 = 700$ patients.
4. Total occupied beds after 2 weeks = $200 \text{ (initial)} + 700 \text{ (new)} = 900$ beds.
5. Remaining unoccupied beds = $1000 - 900 = 100$ beds. (Alternatively, starting with 800 initial unoccupied beds and subtracting the 700 new admissions also yields $800 - 700 = 100$).

The logic is sound and universally agreed upon by the peer models.

Final answer: 100
